title: Orchestrate multi-metric VPC health fabric: unified probes, scoring, and Terraform modules
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
We need a robust, reusable orchestration for VPC deployment health checks that evaluates multiple signals (latency distributions, error rates, GPU/instance saturation, and token throughput) and produces a single per-deployment health score plus per-probe SLO alerts. This ticket designs and implements: 1) a Terraform module to provision monitoring primitives and synthetic probes, 2) a probe orchestration service (lightweight runner) that normalizes signals into a health score, and 3) default SLO policies and alerting rules for private deployments.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Ship terraform modules that create Prometheus exporters/agents, synthetic probes (short warmup + steady-state token throughput tests), exporter configs, and alerting rules (PagerDuty + runbook links).
  - Implement a probe runner on the control plane side that samples per-zone metrics and calculates a rolling health score with explainability (which signal dominated).
  - Provide sane defaults for token throughput and saturation SLOs and a mechanism to tune them per-customer capacity reservation.
- Non-goals:
  - This ticket does not change runtime scheduling or autoscaling decisions. It exposes signals for autoscaler & console to consume (follow-up).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Multi-metric scoring vs independent alerts: we'll emit independent SLO alerts for primary signals (p95 latency, 5xx rate, token throughput drop, GPU util saturation) but also compute a composite health score used in the Console for quick triage. Rationale: many incidents manifest in one dominant signal but operators need a single view for escalation.
- Synthetic probes: two-tier approach — short warmup probe (10s burst) to detect cold-start regressions in KV caching + longer token-rate probe (60s steady-rate) to measure sustainable token throughput. Trade-off: slightly higher probe traffic vs faster detection of regressions.
- Exporter footprint: use resource-limited DaemonSet for on-prem; for cloud hosted private control plane use sidecar exporter. Terraform module will expose variables for mode.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Terraform module: gitlab.com/redwood/infrastructure/terraform/modules/vpc-health-fabric - provisions: PrometheusNodeExporter configs, probe ECS/K8s jobs, alerting rules, IAM roles, and Grafana dashboards as JSON model. Variables for probe cadence, retention, and region selectors.
2) Probe runner service: small Go service in runtime-observability repo that fetches metrics, normalizes (z-score over rolling window), computes composite score [0..100], stores time-series in Prometheus as custom metric (redwood_vpc_health_score).
3) Default SLOs: document and codify p50/p95 latency thresholds, error-rate ceilings, token-throughput baselines per instance type, and saturation thresholds per GPU model. These are configurable in tenant config.
4) Alerts & Runbooks: standard alert templates tied to signals, with auto-attach runbooks in the Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module creates all monitored resources in our staging VPC and can be reused across customers.
- Probe runner publishes redwood_vpc_health_score and per-signal metrics with labels (zone, deployment_id).
- Alerts fire in test scenarios (simulated overload, induced 5xx, artificially limited token rate) and link to runbooks.
- Dashboard surfaces composite score and top contributing signals.

Artifact links and references:
- Proposed Terraform module skeleton: gitlab.com/redwood/infrastructure/terraform/modules/vpc-health-fabric (branch: eng/16984-probes)
- Probe runner prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Design notes and PoC graphs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/1423/VPC+Health+Fabric+Design
- Console dashboard mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcDEF/view

Open questions:
- Should the composite score be weighted to prioritize latency over throughput for PLG customers? (Action: PM to propose weighting presets per customer tier.)
- Do we allow customers to opt their Dedicated pools out of synthetic probes for compliance? (Security flagged this; default: probes run from control plane, no customer data captured.)

Next steps / tasks:
- [ ] Finalize TF module output variables and provider patterns (Marcus, due 2026-02-22).
- [ ] Ship probe runner minimal MVP and wire a Prometheus metric (Aisha, due 2026-03-05).
- [ ] Create Console panel + draft runbooks (Design: Priya Sharma, due 2026-03-12).
- [ ] Security review for synthetic probes and IAM roles (Security team, due 2026-03-18).

Notes on rollout and customer impact:
- Rollout will be staged: first test in internal staging vpc, then opt-in for pilot customers on Dedicated, then on by default for new Private installs after security approval.
- Customer visible telemetry will be namespaced by deployment_id; no payloads or user data leave the VPC.
